data.title: Idempotency
data.tagline: A repeated request produces the same intended business effect instead of applying it again
data.learningOutcome: You can choose a stable request identifier and verify that only one concurrent delivery claims processing and applies the business effect.
data.description: If a payment provider retries the same callback concurrently after a timeout, the order service uses its stable event id as a unique key and atomically claims processing so the order is marked paid only once. Idempotency does not mean zero logs, notifications, or other side effects, and different business operations must not share one key.

learning.assumes: You know that network requests can arrive again after a timeout or retry.
learning.outcome: You can choose a stable request identifier and verify that only one concurrent delivery claims processing and applies the business effect.

distinctions.label: Side Effect
distinctions.explanation: Side Effect describes external state changes caused by an operation; Idempotency guarantees identical outcomes when repeated requests produce side effects only once.

explanation.title: Replace duplicate handling with an atomic claim
explanation.text: The provider may deliver event evt_7f2 concurrently. The server identifies one business action by its event id and uses a unique constraint or equivalent operation to claim processing atomically. Other requests only read the in-progress or saved result without creating or charging again.

explanation.title: How to observe the improvement
explanation.text: Give both first and repeated callbacks a clear result so the caller can stop retrying. After delivering the event concurrently, verify that there is still one order, one payment state change, and a matching trace record.

explanation.title: Another case: repeated form submission
explanation.text: When a slow network makes someone click Create project several times, the client can reuse one idempotency key for that creation. The server atomically claims the key and reuses the first result instead of creating multiple projects.

data.boundary: Idempotency constrains the intended business effect of the same request. A read-then-write check does not stop concurrent duplicates, so processing ownership must be claimed atomically. Logs, audit records, and notifications may still be side effects, and external services need their own idempotency protection.

lessonPractice.title: The same payment callback is sent twice after a timeout. Which handling is appropriate?

options.label: Use a stable event id and unique constraint to claim processing atomically; reuse the result for repeats
options.feedback: Correct. The stable id identifies one business action, the atomic claim prevents two concurrent handlers from starting it, and the saved result gives retries a consistent response.

options.label: Return as fast as possible and ask the payment provider never to retry
options.feedback: You cannot control packet loss or provider retries; without server-side deduplication, the order can still change twice.

options.label: Accept only by arrival time and treat a later callback as a new order
options.feedback: Arrival time is not business identity; the same callback can arrive later and still be processed twice.

data.agentPrompt: Make the payment callback idempotent: use the provider's stable event id as a unique key and claim processing with a unique constraint or equivalent atomic operation before the business effect. Return an already-processing or saved result for repeats without creating or charging twice. Deliver the same callback concurrently at least twice and verify that one request gains ownership and only one business state change occurs. Protect the external charge with the same idempotency key or an equivalent mechanism.
